comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 18. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 18 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '28'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn a life through $436A, poll status/input through $436D, and test bombs remaining at $3013. Zero bombs calls cleanup and jumps through completion vector $3030. Death mode 2 waits to become 0; reserves $40E4=$FF calls cleanup and jumps through exhaustion vector $3032, otherwise respawn. Cleanup vector $301D is invoked through a patched JSR.
IRQ collision callback: when player-active $402B and player collision mask $4088 are nonzero and player mode $4028 is 0, set mode 1 to begin death. Any colliding sprite is lethal here.

Drawing data $30A4-$3143 read by Initial scenery $30A4. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

18 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.
Four cardinal entries in each component array: X-low 0,4,0,$FC; X-high 0,0,0,$FF; Y $FE,0,2,0. Route selection copies a chosen vector to the robot workspace.

Drawing data $31CF-$31E2 read by Post-bomb drawing $31CF, Post-bomb drawing $31D9. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

Write duration16 to up entry$3330 (already16) and down entry$3366 (initially0). Only the downward node12(128,120) to18(128,152) edge is newly opened; reverse up was already available. CPU executes full bomb path and16-step traversal both ways. The bomb also requests its separate geometry change.

Write16 to up$3331 (already16) and down$3368 (initially0). Newly opens down node14(224,120) to19(224,152), retaining existing reverse up. Directed edges70 initially,71 after either callback,72 after both. CPU checked full collector/postdraw and both-direction traversals.
Three X-low values 48,176,48; three X-high values 0,0,1; three Y values 184,120,184. Initialization uses biased bases $31F0/$31F3/$31F6 with sprite indices 5-7.

Four packed 30-byte robot frames, expanded to VIC frames $10-$13. The generic copier always reads 240 bytes; only the first 120 are these frames. The following bytes enter unused frames and are not part of the animation.
Expand frames at $31FE through $4376, then initialize sprites 5-7 from position table $31F5 with frame $10, colour 7, enabled.
Eight-byte sprite-indexed workspace holding remaining updates on the chosen edge. Only robot slots 5-7 are processed.
Eight-byte sprite-indexed workspace holding signed X velocity low byte. Only robot slots 5-7 are processed.
Eight-byte sprite-indexed workspace holding signed X velocity high byte. Only robot slots 5-7 are processed.
Eight-byte sprite-indexed workspace holding signed Y velocity. Only robot slots 5-7 are processed.
Thirty navigation-node X low coordinates. At the end of a movement, a robot must match all three coordinates of a node before choosing another edge.
Thirty navigation-node X high coordinates. At the end of a movement, a robot must match all three coordinates of a node before choosing another edge.
Thirty navigation-node Y coordinates. At the end of a movement, a robot must match all three coordinates of a node before choosing another edge.
Thirty node-indexed up edge durations. Zero means no passage; a positive value is the number of movement updates to the next node. Bomb callbacks modify selected up/down entries to open connections.

Thirty node-indexed right edge durations. Zero means no passage; a positive value is the number of movement updates to the next node. Bomb callbacks modify selected up/down entries to open connections.

Thirty node-indexed down edge durations. Zero means no passage; a positive value is the number of movement updates to the next node. Bomb callbacks modify selected up/down entries to open connections.

Thirty node-indexed left edge durations. Zero means no passage; a positive value is the number of movement updates to the next node. Bomb callbacks modify selected up/down entries to open connections.

During active play, animate frames $10+$4025 and process three robots. An existing movement continues through $345C. Otherwise scan 30 nodes for an exact X-low/X-high/Y match, save its index, and fall into direction selection at $33E2. A robot at no known node waits in place.
Four bytes: saved robot slot, random direction 0-3, current node 0-29, and flattened direction*30+node route-table offset.

At a node try one original-RNG direction per eligible update; missing/disallowed choice waits. Vertical preference up if playerY smaller else down; horizontal right if playerhalfX greater else left. Equality permits down/left. Once accepted, finish entire edge countdown without retargeting. CPU checked4800 choices across all30 nodes/four opening states. Accepted edges load cardinal velocity/duration and move immediately.

During active play outside mode 2, any robot collision mask $408D-$408F containing robot bits $E0 randomizes frequency-high and duration bytes $34C5/$34C6 in sound $34BE. Queue this pulse chirp at priority 2; duration becomes (random&7)+1.

Mutable SID chirp: envelope $00/$00, pulse $8888, frequency low byte 4, randomized high byte $34C5, randomized duration $34C6, then zero terminator. The collision callback writes both randomized fields.
